thread.title: Mary Meeker: The 'Privacy Paradox' of Tech and Personal Data

author: Barron's
title: Mary Meeker: The 'Privacy Paradox' of Tech and Personal Data
text:
Getty Images/iStockphoto Mary Meeker's annual report on Internet trends is always a page turner. Or, to be more precise, a slide-turner, as in 294 of them.
In covering everything from flat smartphone shipments to tech's growing economic power and the Chinese market, she warned that tech companies face a "privacy paradox." They're using more data to enrich their customers' experiences without betraying their trust.
"Scrutiny is rising on all sides--users, businesses, regulators," Meeker, a partner at Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers , said in a presentation at the Code Conference in Rancho Palos Verdes in southern California today. "Technology-driven trends are changing so rapidly that it's rare when one side fully understands the other, setting the stage for reactions that can have unintended consequences."
Meeker said the number of Internet users, 3.6 billion, surpassed half the planet's population. "When markets reach mainstream, new growth gets harder to find--evinced by 0% new smartphone unit-shipment growth in 2017," she said.
Last year, she said, marked the first time smartphone shipments did not grow. A key reason may be cost: Despite new, high-profile $1,000 phones from Apple (ticker: AAPL) and Samsung Electronics (South Korea: 005930), the average selling price of smartphones again declined globally. Meanwhile, lower-cost smartphones continued to gain traction in less-developed markets, Meeker said.
One country benefiting from the explosion of low-cost mobile phones is China , where it led the world in mobile-payment adoption with more than 500 million active users last year.
Stateside, the influence of tech on the economy deepened. In April, the industry accounted for 25% of U.S. market capitalization, she said. E-commerce sales, meanwhile, grew 16% in the U.S. last year, compared with 14% in 2016. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) was the big winner, with 28% of the e-commerce market, contributing to a drop in physical retail sales.
